description: The specification you give an assistant: goal, stack, architecture, contract (statuses and bodies), rules, non-functional needs, constraints, deliverables, out of scope.
One endpoint or module generated, run and reviewed at a time, instead of a whole system in one prompt.
A default choice per backend problem plus the conditions that justify switching, so you decide before the assistant does.
Contract, validation, security, data, reliability, maintainability and tests: the questions to ask of every generated change.
A package, method or option that does not exist (or no longer exists) but appears plausible in generated code.
Attackers publish packages under names assistants tend to invent, so blindly installing suggested dependencies installs malware.
A committed file (`CLAUDE.md`, rules) describing stack, layers and conventions so every session starts with the same context.
